_note: Onboarding and process content for new and future clients. Items with clauses cite the NMC document. Items with b:'interp' are our recommended practice. Checkbox IDs must stay stable because ticks are stored in the browser by ID.

items.t: Confirm the client type: individual doctor, clinic or hospital, or other (wellness, diagnostics)
Identify the State Medical Council and any State Clinical Establishments Act that applies
Collect each doctor's name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR number, with a copy of the certificate
Complete the client intake questionnaire (below)
Audit existing site, ads, social, GBP and listings against the Fix-now register
Send the client a written list of what we will not publish and why, and get acknowledgement
Agree who at the client approves content, and how (email or approval tool)
Record all awards, rankings and accreditations with proof
Record device and equipment names, and the basis of any approval claim
Check for existing patient consent records for any material we may be given
Confirm we will not run influencer, review or offer campaigns
Confirm the fee model does not link payment to individual patients
Set up forms, consent text and privacy notice
Set up the approval workflow and the shared record folder

intake.title: Client intake questionnaire
intake.intro: Send this to the client before any work starts. We keep the answers in the client folder.

questions.q: Full name of each doctor as on the register
questions.why: Identity details must be shown on electronic posts.

questions.q: Qualifications of each doctor, as recognised
questions.why: Shown with the name.

questions.q: Registration status and SMR/NMR number, and which council
questions.why: Must be disclosed. We will check against the register.

questions.q: Legal name of the clinic or hospital, and its registration under the Clinical Establishments Act or State Act (if any)
questions.why: Clinics are governed by that law.

questions.q: Who is the authorised person to approve content?
questions.why: The doctor or clinic is responsible for what they authorise.

questions.q: Which departments, facilities, emergency services and accreditations can we state, with certificates?
questions.why: Factual and verifiable particulars only.

questions.q: Names of equipment and technology to mention, and their intended use
questions.why: Allowed as fact, with no superiority claims.

questions.q: Consultation fees and package charges to display
questions.why: Fee disclosure must be factual and not misleading.

questions.q: Any awards, rankings or media features, with the awarding body, date, methodology and proof
questions.why: Must be independently verifiable.

questions.q: Any journal-published research by the doctor
questions.why: Research-based communication is an allowed exception.

questions.q: Photos or videos of doctors that the client wants used, and where
questions.why: Doctor photos can be a problem if promotional.

questions.q: Do you hold any patient photos, videos, reviews or stories? Where are they used today?
questions.why: We need to find and remove prohibited content.

questions.q: For any patient material, what consent was recorded, and when?
questions.why: Consent must be specific, informed, voluntary and documented, and still does not legalise prohibited uses.

questions.q: Will patients appear in clinic footage?
questions.why: Identifiable patients must not be shown.

questions.q: List all live websites, landing pages, ad accounts, social profiles, GBP and directory listings
questions.why: We audit all of them.

questions.q: Any agencies, influencers, PR firms or platforms currently engaged, and how they are paid
questions.why: Payment linked to patients is restricted.

questions.q: Any paid ranking or featured listings on healthcare platforms
questions.why: Platforms must not rank doctors for payment.

questions.q: Any review-request practices (QR codes, WhatsApp, front desk, incentives)?
questions.why: Soliciting reviews is restricted.

questions.q: Do you use AI tools for content, images or replies?
questions.why: AI content needs a source mark and must not mislead.

questions.q: What patient or enquiry data do you want used for ads, email or WhatsApp?
questions.why: Personal data must follow data-protection law.

questions.q: What consent and privacy notices are in place?
questions.why: Consent must be documented.

workflow.title: Suggested approval workflow
workflow.intro: Our suggestion for who checks what before anything goes live. This is our recommended practice, not something the NMC document sets out.

steps.what: Makes the deliverable and runs the QA checklist for that type
Peer-checks the deliverable against the checklist and the playbook
Checks identity details, proofs for claims, consent records and that the client's approver is right
Approves in writing. This is the record that the client authorised the content
Decides grey-area items: verifiable superlatives, awards, scientific cases, free consultations, doctor photos, fee models
Publishes. Files the approval and the QA checklist in the client folder

contract.title: Contract and scope-of-work points to discuss with leadership
contract.intro: These are discussion points for Leadership and legal counsel, not drafted clauses. All of them are our suggestions.

points.t: Client responsibility for content: state that the client (doctor or clinic) approves all content and is responsible for the accuracy of claims, registration details and consents they supply
Right to refuse: we may decline or pause work that would breach the NMC Guidelines or other applicable law, without it being a breach of contract
Written approval: no deliverable goes live without written approval; the approval log is kept
Out of scope: testimonials, review campaigns, before-and-after, influencer work, offer campaigns and AI-generated people, listed as outside scope
Fee structure: review any fee linked to leads, bookings or patients, and take legal advice on whether to restructure
Information from the client: the client supplies registration numbers, qualifications, proofs for awards and accreditations, and consent records
Data protection: roles and responsibilities for personal data used in forms, ads and messaging
Regulatory change: how we handle new NMC clarifications and State Council rules, and who pays for resulting rework
Takedown: we may remove content at any time if we believe it breaches the Guidelines
